prerequisites: Mathematics I and II of Bachillerato

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering.
Aptitude to apply knowledge about: differential and integral calculus.
Ability to solve problems within their area of study
Ability to abstract: ability to create and use models that reflect real situations.
Ability to plan and organize personal work.
Ability to integrate quickly and work efficiently in unidisciplinary teams and to collaborate in a multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to communicate effectively (in expression and comprehension) orally and in writing, with special emphasis on writing technical documentation.
Possess the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies or improve their training with a certain degree of autonomy.
Have motivation for quality and continuous improvement and act with rigor in professional development.
Operate and represent real functions of a real variable, obtain their limits, determine their continuity, calculate derivatives and formulate and solve optimization problems.
Manage the concepts of sequences and series and use power series to represent functions.
Formulate and calculate integrals of single-variable functions and apply them to solve engineering-related problems.
State and apply the basic properties of real functions of several real variables. Obtain their limits, analyze continuity and differentiability and solve optimization problems.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK 1: REAL FUNCTIONS OF ONE REAL VARIABLE

Topic 1: Numerical Sets and Functions. Natural numbers: Induction method. Real numbers. Absolute value of a real number. Properties. Elementary functions. Composition of functions and inverse function.

Topic 2: Limits and continuity. Definition of limit. Properties. Infinitesimals and infinities. Indeterminations. Asymptotes. Continuous functions. Properties of continuous functions: Bolzano's theorem, Darboux's theorem (intermediate value) and Weierstrass's theorem.

Topic 3: Differentiability. Properties of differentiable functions. Derivative of a function at a point. Derivative function. Differentiability and continuity. Properties of the derivative. Chain rule. Rolle's theorem. Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem. L’Hôpital's rule.
Topic 4: Taylor Polynomial. Successive derivatives. Taylor polynomial. Taylor formula with remainder.
Topic 5: Optimization. Local study of a function. Monotonicity, relative extrema, concavity and inflection points. Absolute extrema. Graphical representation of functions.
BLOCK 2: RIEMANN INTEGRAL
Topic 1: Calculation of antiderivatives. Immediate integrals. Integration methods.

Topic 2: The definite integral. Basic concepts and geometric interpretation. Integrable functions. Properties of the definite integral. Fundamental theorem of integral calculus. Barrow's rule. Applications.
Topic 3: Improper integrals. Definition of improper integral. Types. Application to the study of Eulerian integrals.
BLOCK 3: SEQUENCES AND SERIES. POWER SERIES
Topic 1: Numerical sequences. Definition. Convergence. Limit calculation.
Topic 2: Numerical series. Definition. Convergence and sum. Harmonic series and geometric series. Convergence criteria.
Topic 3: Power series. Power series expansion. Definition. Radius of convergence. Differentiation and integration. Power series expansion of a function: Taylor series. Common expansions.
BLOCK 4: FUNCTIONS OF SEVERAL VARIABLES
Topic 1: The Euclidean space Rn. Basic notions of topology in Rn. Real functions. Vector functions.
Topic 2: Limits and continuity. Limit of a function at a point and properties. Limit calculation. Continuity of a function. Properties.
Topic 3: Differentiability. Directional derivative. Partial derivative. Geometric interpretation. Higher-order derivatives. Differentiation and continuity.
Topic 4: Differentiation. Differential of a function at a point. Linear approximation. Sufficient condition for differentiability. Gradient vector. Tangent plane. Chain rule.
Topic 5: Optimization. Free relative extrema. Necessary condition. Sufficient condition. Absolute extrema. Conditional relative extrema. Lagrange multipliers.
PRACTICES
Introduction. Basic notions of the program.
Differential Calculus. Calculation of limits and derivatives. Graphical representations. Calculation of the Taylor Polynomial. Solving optimization problems.
Integral Calculus. Calculation of antiderivatives, definite integrals and improper integrals. Calculation of area and volumes.
Sequences and series. Limits of sequences. Study of convergence and sum of series. Calculation of the radius of convergence of a power series.
Functions of several variables. Graphical representations. Study of function behavior.
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) in the ordinary call is calculated as NF = 0.15 NL + max(0.15 NA + 0.7 NC, 0.85 NC), where NL is the laboratory practices grade, NA is the classroom practices grade, and NC is the average of the partial exams ((P1 + P2)/2) or the global exam grade (PG). The course is passed if NF >= 5 and NC >= 3.5. If these minimums are not met, the final grade will be min(NF, NC). For extraordinary calls, students can retake an written exam for NC and/or a laboratory practices test for NL; the highest grade for each part is kept.
